issue: Lead 'Capital Modeling Actuary' and supporting 'Catastrophe (CAT) Modeler' (used on S01–S05 of RF-21-03) are not in role-inventory.json.
proposedFix: Rename to the inventory roles: lead 'Capital Model Actuary', supporting 'CAT Modeler' on all five steps of RF-21-03.
rationale: Role names must resolve against the 261-role inventory; these are near-miss variants of existing roles ('Capital Model Actuary', 'CAT Modeler'), so role-based drill-downs and I/O resolution will silently miss these steps. Verified: both variants appear on all five steps and neither resolves.

issue: Supporting role 'Statutory Accountant' does not exist in role-inventory.json.
proposedFix: Replace with 'Statutory Reporting Analyst' (or 'Statutory Reporting Manager').
rationale: Booking reserves into statutory financials is performed with the statutory reporting team; the inventory's equivalent roles are Statutory Reporting Analyst/Manager — the current name will not resolve.

issue: Supporting role 'CFO' is an abbreviation not present in role-inventory.json; similarly RF-21-02-S01 supporting includes 'Data Analyst', which is also not in the inventory.
proposedFix: S05: replace 'CFO' with 'Chief Financial Officer'. S01: replace 'Data Analyst' with 'Actuarial Technician' (or 'Data Engineer').
rationale: Both names fail to match the role inventory, breaking role-to-step resolution; the inventory contains the canonical equivalents ('Chief Financial Officer', 'Actuarial Technician', 'Data Engineer').

issue: The Appointed Actuary leads all five steps of routine portfolio performance monitoring and assumption refresh (RF-21-04-S01–S05).
proposedFix: Make 'Pricing Actuary' (or 'Reserving Actuary') the lead for day-to-day monitoring/assumption refresh, with 'Appointed Actuary' and 'Chief Actuary' supporting/reviewing.
rationale: The Appointed Actuary is a Board-appointed statutory officer responsible for the reserve opinion, not the day-to-day operator of quarterly portfolio monitoring; leads should be the roles that run the step day-to-day. Practitioners would also flag the independence optics of the opinion-signer owning the assumption refresh end-to-end.

issue: 'Premium Auditor' is the supporting role on every step of RC-19-01, RC-19-02 and RC-19-04. Premium audit is a policyholder exposure/payroll audit function within underwriting/billing operations — not internal audit staff.
proposedFix: Replace 'Premium Auditor' with 'Audit Associate' as the supporting role across RC-19-01, RC-19-02 and RC-19-04 (and add 'Audit Associate' to RC-19-03, which currently has supporting 'None').
rationale: Using a first-line operational role as internal audit engagement staff violates IIA independence/objectivity standards (Attribute Standards 1100/1120) and is a clear miscast — the inventory already contains the correct 'Audit Associate' role. Verified: Premium Auditor supports all steps of RC-19-01/02/04 and RC-19-03 has no supporting role.

issue: RC-19-01 (Risk-based audit planning) uses the fieldwork step template — 'Gather Evidence', 'Assess & Test', 'Document Findings', 'Report & Remediate' — even though the L4's output is an annual audit plan, not testing results.
proposedFix: Rename the planning steps to planning-appropriate verbs, e.g. S02 'Assess Audit Universe & Risks', S03 'Prioritize Engagements & Resources', S04 'Draft Annual Audit Plan', S05 'Publish Audit Plan & Schedule'.
rationale: IIA Standard 2010 planning produces a risk-based plan via risk assessment and prioritization; 'Assess & Test'/'Report & Remediate' describe engagement execution and will mislead anyone navigating the model (the same names appear correctly in RC-19-02 fieldwork). Verified: S05's outputs are 'Audit plan, scope, audit universe priorities, engagement schedule' under a 'Report & Remediate' label.

issue: Supporting roles list both 'SRE' and 'Site Reliability Engineer' — the same role under two inventory aliases — on every step of TD-28-03 and TD-28-07.
proposedFix: Keep one ('SRE', the name used as lead elsewhere in this stream) and replace the duplicate with a genuinely distinct supporter, e.g. 'IT Service Delivery Manager' for TD-28-03 and 'Platform Engineering Lead' for TD-28-07.
rationale: Duplicate-alias role assignments inflate role-participation counts and signal a copy/paste defect; the role inventory's duplication of SRE/Site Reliability Engineer should not be propagated onto a single step. Verified: both aliases appear together on all steps of TD-28-03 and TD-28-07, and the proposed replacements exist in the inventory.

issue: All five steps of 'Recovery collection, settlement and closeout' (CI-26-04-S01..S05) are led by 'Reinsurance Claims / Recoveries Specialist', but this L4 is direct subrogation/third-party recovery collection. Reinsurance recoverables are already owned end-to-end by CI-05-04 'Claims recovery and program performance reporting' (verified: Reinsurance Analyst/Manager track, bill, collect and reconcile reinsurer balances there).
proposedFix: Change leads on CI-26-04-S01 through S05 to 'Collections Recovery Specialist' (or 'Subrogation Specialist'), keeping 'Subrogation / Litigation Specialist' as supporting.
rationale: Direct subrogation collection (demands on adverse carriers/parties, payment plans, intercompany arbitration awards) is performed by subrogation/collections staff, not the reinsurance recoverables team; the current assignment conflates two distinct recovery flows that the model otherwise correctly separates. Both proposed role names verified present in role-inventory.json.

issue: 'Receive Customer Contact' (accept inbound inquiry via any channel) duplicates the entire OC-14-01 L4 'Contact intake and case routing', whose S05 output is already 'Logged interaction, routed case, service priority, first-contact response'. The resolution L4 re-performs intake instead of consuming the routed case.
proposedFix: Rename/redefine OC-14-02-S01 as 'Review Routed Case & Confirm Scope' with inputs 'Routed case, service priority (from OC-14-01)' and output 'Confirmed service request'.
rationale: Industry contact-center reference models (intake/route then resolve) keep channel intake in one place; the duplication creates two competing systems of record for the same interaction and breaks the L4-to-L4 handoff the outline itself defines in OC-14-01-S05.

issue: Roles across OC-14-01 (S01–S05) and OC-14-02 (S01–S06) are not in the role inventory (all verified absent): 'Customer Service Representative (CSR)', 'Customer Service Representative', 'Contact Center Operations Manager', 'Contact Center Supervisor', 'Subject Matter Expert', 'Claims/Billing/UW Specialist', 'Quality Analyst', 'Customer Experience Manager'.
proposedFix: Map to exact inventory names: 'Customer Service Rep' (leads), 'Contact Center Ops Manager' (supervisor/ops manager), 'Senior Contact Center Agent' (escalation), 'Quality Assurance Analyst (Service)' (QA), 'Customer Experience Lead' (CX), and concrete specialists ('Claims Analyst', 'Billing Analyst', 'Underwriting Assistant') instead of 'Claims/Billing/UW Specialist' and 'Subject Matter Expert'.
rationale: Steps whose leads/supporting are free-text variants break the role-resolution chain (deliverables/tasks resolve by exact role-name match), so these steps will show no owners in role drill-downs and workforce analytics. All proposed replacement names verified present in role-inventory.json. Note 'Contact Center Operations Manager' also appears in OC-14-04-S01..S05 supporting and should be fixed there in the same pass.

issue: All five steps of 'Security architecture and control definition' (TR-25-01-S01..S05) use 'ISO Security Architect' (lead) and 'Chief Information Security Officer' (supporting), neither of which is in the role inventory; the inventory has 'ISO Architect' and 'Chief Info Security Officer' (both verified).
proposedFix: Change leads on TR-25-01-S01 through S05 to 'ISO Architect' and supporting to 'Application Security Lead, Chief Info Security Officer'.
rationale: Near-miss role names silently orphan the steps from role-based views; exact inventory names restore the linkage with no semantic change.

issue: The IAM L4 (TR-25-02) uses roles not in the inventory (all verified absent): 'Requesting Manager' (S01 lead), 'Data Owner' (S02/S04 lead), 'IT Support' (S03 supporting), 'Internal Auditor' (S06 lead).
proposedFix: Map to inventory roles: 'Operations Manager' or 'HR Business Partner' for the requesting line manager, 'Data Steward' for Data Owner, 'IT Service Desk Analyst' for IT Support, 'Internal Audit' for Internal Auditor.
rationale: The process logic (request → approve → provision → certify → revoke → audit) is sound and matches SOX/NYDFS access-control expectations, but the actor names must resolve against the 261-role inventory for the model to be usable in role drill-downs and access-review accountability reporting. All proposed replacements verified present in role-inventory.json.

issue: 'SOC Analyst' (lead on TR-25-03-S01/S02, supporting on S03) and 'IT Operations' (supporting on S04) are not in the role inventory (verified); the inventory has 'Security Analyst', 'SOC Lead', and infrastructure roles.
proposedFix: Replace 'SOC Analyst' with 'Security Analyst' and 'IT Operations' with 'Infrastructure / Network Engineer' (or 'IT Service Delivery Manager') on TR-25-03-S01 through S04.
rationale: Same role-resolution defect as above: the SOC monitoring/triage steps will not surface under any real role, which understates the Security Analyst workload in the operating model. Proposed replacements verified present in role-inventory.json.

issue: The Chief Data Officer is named day-to-day lead of all five Data Product Intake steps (S01–S05), including Build & Configure — an executive cannot be the operational lead for requirements capture and build work.
proposedFix: Make Data Architect the lead for S01–S04 (supporting: Data Steward, BI / Analytics Manager), reserving Chief Data Officer as lead/approver only on S05 Approve & Publish.
rationale: Operating models distinguish accountable executives from process operators; CDO-as-lead on every step makes the RACI unusable for staffing and contradicts how the other TD-24 L4s assign working-level leads (Data Quality Manager, Data Steward). All replacement roles verified present in role-inventory.json.

issue: Supporting role 'Business Unit Heads' is not in the 261-role inventory; the same defect recurs in this L4: S03 supporting 'Data Analyst', S04 supporting 'Business SME', S06 supporting 'Data Governance Committee' — none are inventory roles (verified against the outline and inventory).
proposedFix: S02 supporting → 'Data Governance, Data Steward'; S03 supporting → 'Data Steward, BI / Analytics Manager'; S04 supporting → 'Data Engineer, Data Steward'; S06 supporting → 'Data Governance'.
rationale: Role-resolved views (deliverable→role→task chains) silently drop steps whose roles do not match the inventory; the inventory already contains the correct equivalents ('Data Governance' is a named role).

issue: 'Verify Licensing & Credentials' checks licenses only; professional indemnity (E&O) cover and premium trust/bank account details — mandatory items in Lloyd's coverholder due diligence and annual compliance — are absent from inputs and outputs.
proposedFix: Extend inputs to 'Licensing status, state requirements, E&O/professional indemnity certificates, premium trust account details' and outputs to 'License verification report, E&O cover confirmation, bank/trust account verification'.
rationale: Lloyd's coverholder approval and annual compliance explicitly cover professional indemnity, licences, financials and bank accounts; an authority granted to a partner with lapsed PI cover is a material E&O and regulatory exposure.

issue: Routine, ongoing control testing within Operational Oversight is led by 'Internal Auditor' — a role not in the inventory ('Internal Audit' is the inventory name) — and assigning internal audit as first-line operator of a recurring control conflicts with IIA Three Lines independence, since the same function then audits this activity in CI-03-04-S01.
proposedFix: Lead → 'Delegated Authority Analyst' (inventory role), supporting → 'Compliance Analyst, Delegated Authority Manager'; reserve 'Internal Audit' for the periodic audit steps in CI-03-04 (and correct the 'Internal Auditor' spelling there and in CI-03-02-S03 supporting).
rationale: Under the IIA Three Lines Model, management (first line) performs day-to-day control monitoring and internal audit (third line) provides independent periodic assurance; the current assignment destroys audit independence over delegated authority oversight. Verified 'Internal Auditor' is absent from the inventory while 'Internal Audit' and 'Delegated Authority Analyst' exist.

issue: Lead 'Data Analyst' is not in the role inventory, while the inventory contains the purpose-built 'Bordereaux Analyst' role that exists precisely for bordereaux validation; same substitution applies to the 'Data Analyst' supporting entries in CI-03-03-S01 and CI-03-02-S04 (all three occurrences verified in the outline).
proposedFix: Replace 'Data Analyst' with 'Bordereaux Analyst' as lead of S02 and as supporting in CI-03-03-S01 and CI-03-02-S04.
rationale: Bordereaux validation is the defining task of the Bordereaux Analyst role in the inventory; using a non-inventory generic role breaks role-resolved navigation and orphans the real role.
sources: Lloyd's delegated authority reporting standards (Coverholder Reporting Standards v5)

issue: 'Onboard Producers' (S02) and 'Train on Products' (S03) inside Pipeline Development duplicate the entire PG-16-02 Partner Enablement L4 ('Broker/MGA onboarding and enablement' — whose outputs already include onboarded partner, enablement pack, training and access setup), creating two competing onboarding flows with no handoff between them.
proposedFix: Refocus PG-16-03 on pipeline activities (recruit → set goals → activate → monitor → compensate) and route recruited producers into PG-16-02 for contracting, setup and training: replace S02 with a handoff step 'Refer Producer to Onboarding (PG-16-02)' or fold S02/S03 content into PG-16-02 and renumber.
rationale: Duplicate onboarding paths mean the regulatory controls added to PG-16-02 (screening, appointments) can be bypassed via the PG-16-03 path; a single producer-lifecycle flow is the industry norm in producer management platforms.

issue: PG-16-03 is saturated with roles absent from the inventory: S06 lead 'Producer Relations Manager' and supporting 'Commissions Analyst, AP Specialist'; also S01 'Territory Manager'/'Marketing Manager', S02 'IT Support', S03 'Training Manager'/'Product Manager', S04/S05 'Territory Manager' (every occurrence verified against the outline and inventory).
proposedFix: Map to inventory roles: S06 lead → 'Commission Analyst', supporting → 'Distribution Operations Manager, Channel Operations Coordinator'; 'Producer Relations Manager' → 'Agency Relations Manager'; 'Territory Manager' → 'Sales / Distribution Analyst' or 'Business Dev Manager'; 'Marketing Manager' → 'Marketing Coordinator'; 'Training Manager' → 'Training Coordinator'; 'Product Manager' → 'Insurance Product Manager'; 'IT Support' → 'IT Service Desk Analyst'.
rationale: Every step in this L4 fails role-inventory validation, so the whole Pipeline Development sub-process disappears from role-based views and staffing analyses; the inventory contains direct equivalents for each role (note the inventory spelling is 'Commission Analyst', singular).

issue: Step 'Manage Liquidity' (inputs: cash flows/investments; output: liquidity position) duplicates the entire F-11-03 L4 'Cash, liquidity and funding management' and is off-topic inside an L4 named 'Capital actions, tax and solvency reporting'. Meanwhile no step in F-11-04 actually executes capital actions, which the L4 name promises — verified: the only other 'capital actions' reference in the model is RF-21-03-S05 (Actuarial Capital Modeling), which outputs capital actions as model recommendations, not execution.
proposedFix: Replace with 'Execute Capital Actions': plan and execute shareholder/parent dividends (including 30-day prior notice or approval for extraordinary dividends under the state Holding Company Act), capital contributions and surplus notes. Lead: Treasury Manager; supporting: Capital Management Manager, Chief Financial Officer.
rationale: NAIC Insurance Holding Company System Regulatory Act (Model #440) requires commissioner notice/approval for extraordinary dividends and reporting of all dividends — a regulated capital-action process every US insurer must run, currently absent (zero hits for 'dividend' or 'surplus note' anywhere in the outline). Removing the liquidity duplicate also resolves double-ownership of the liquidity output between F-11-03 and F-11-04, and the new step becomes the natural consumer of RF-21-03-S05's recommended capital actions. All three replacement roles verified exact in the inventory.

issue: Lead 'Statutory Accountant' is not in the 261-role inventory (verified: also lead on F-11-04-S06 and supporting on F-11-01-S04). Role resolution (roleMatch on leads/supporting) will fail for these steps.
proposedFix: Use 'Statutory Reporting Analyst' as lead (preparer) with 'Statutory Reporting Manager' supporting on F-11-01-S04, F-11-01-S06 and F-11-04-S06.
rationale: Verified both 'Statutory Reporting Analyst' and 'Statutory Reporting Manager' exist in role-inventory.json and 'Statutory Accountant' does not; the invented role breaks the role-to-step linkage the platform resolves at query time on exactly the three steps cited.
sources: role-inventory.json (Statutory Reporting Analyst / Statutory Reporting Manager)

issue: Lead 'Department Managers' is a generic placeholder, not a role in the inventory (verified); the step has no resolvable owner.
proposedFix: Lead: 'FP&A Manager' (facilitates and owns the bottoms-up budget build); supporting: 'Operations Manager, Financial Analyst' as the cost-center-owner representatives.
rationale: Every L5 step must resolve to inventory roles for the deliverable/role/task chain to work; all three replacement roles verified exact in role-inventory.json, and FP&A facilitating department budget builds matches standard FP&A operating practice.

issue: Lead 'CEO' and supporting 'CFO, Board of Directors' are not in the role inventory (verified; likewise 'CEO, Business Unit Heads' on F-11-02-S05, 'BU Heads' on F-11-04-S03, and bare 'CFO' on F-11-01-S05, F-11-02-S01 and F-11-04-S01/S03/S04/S05 vs the inventory's 'Chief Financial Officer').
proposedFix: Replace shorthand with canonical inventory names across F-11: lead F-11-02-S06 = 'Chief Financial Officer', supporting 'Chief Operating Officer, Board Governance Lead'; replace 'BU Heads'/'Business Unit Heads' with 'Chief Underwriting Officer, Chief Operating Officer'; replace bare 'CFO' with 'Chief Financial Officer'.
rationale: Verified these free-text executive shorthands exist exactly as described and break role resolution; there is no 'CEO' or 'Board of Directors' role in the inventory and 'Board Governance Lead' is the inventory's board-facing role (it already leads EM-10-04). All replacement names verified character-exact against role-inventory.json.

issue: The Chief Product Officer is the day-to-day lead of all five demand-shaping/prioritization steps (S01–S05). Intake, scoring and sequencing are operational portfolio activities; a C-suite officer is the decision-maker, not the step operator.
proposedFix: Lead: 'Program Mgmt Office' for S01–S05 (portfolio operations function per SAFe LPM), with 'Chief Product Officer, Chief Technology Officer, Chief Operating Officer' as supporting decision-makers.
rationale: SAFe Lean Portfolio Management assigns portfolio operations (intake, WSJF scoring, Kanban management, sync facilitation) to the ePMO/VMO with executives participating in decision forums; modeling executives as operators distorts the workload and RACI views the platform derives from leads. Amended from the original proposal: supporting role corrected from 'Chief Operating Officer (COO)' to the inventory-exact 'Chief Operating Officer' (the parenthetical form is not in role-inventory.json).

issue: L4 'Commitment & rate optimization (RIs/Savings Plans)' uses the incident-response step template (Detect & Log → Triage & Assign → Investigate & Act → Resolve & Verify → Close & Report) — verified in the outline. Commitment purchasing is a deliberate planning/decision cycle, not an event-driven flow, and the template hides the required financial-approval gate before multi-year spend commitments.
proposedFix: Rename the five steps to a decision-cycle pattern: Analyze Usage & Coverage → Model Commitment Options → Approve Commitment Purchase (Finance/Treasury sign-off) → Execute Purchase → Track Coverage & Utilization. Keep existing leads (FinOps Lead) with Treasury Manager supporting the approval step (Treasury Manager is already in the L4's supporting cast).
rationale: FinOps Foundation Rate Optimization capability describes an analyze-recommend-approve-purchase-track cadence; reserved instances and savings plans are 1–3 year financial obligations, so the approval gate is a control a CFO organization would expect to see named explicitly. Sibling L4s T-27-05/T-27-08 legitimately keep the event-driven template (rightsizing findings, anomaly alerts), so the fix is correctly scoped to T-27-04 only.

issue: L4 F-12-04 is titled 'Portfolio monitoring and investment reporting' (L3 Performance & Risk Reporting) but its steps S01-S04 are actually policy setting, opportunity analysis, trade execution, and settlement. S01 'Set Investment Policy' duplicates F-12-01, whose finalized output is already 'Investment policy, allocation targets, mandate constraints'; S02 'Analyze Opportunities' overlaps F-12-02 security selection.
proposedFix: Remove S01 (consume 'Investment policy' from F-12-01's output as an input instead) and retitle the L4 to 'Trade execution, settlement, valuation and investment reporting' so the execution/settlement steps it uniquely contains are honestly labeled; alternatively move S02 into F-12-02.
rationale: Trade execution and settlement exist nowhere else in the model, so they must stay — but a duplicated policy-setting step creates two competing sources for the same governing document, and the current L4/L3 naming hides the only execution-and-settlement flow under a 'reporting' label.

issue: Lead 'Chief Investment Officer (CIO)' does not match any role-inventory name (inventory has 'Chief Investment Officer'); the same invalid token is used on every step of F-12-01, F-12-02 (supporting), and F-12-03.
proposedFix: Normalize the role to 'Chief Investment Officer' across F-12-01-S01..S05, F-12-02-S01..S05 (supporting), and F-12-03-S01..S05.
rationale: Role names that don't match the inventory break role-based drill-downs and RACI reporting; this is a data-fidelity defect, not a stylistic choice.

issue: Lead 'CFO' and supporting 'Board' are not role-inventory names ('CFO' should be 'Chief Financial Officer'; 'Board' is a governance body, not a role). The same invalid 'CFO, Board' tokens also appear as supporting on F-12-04-S06 'Report Performance'.
proposedFix: S01: lead = 'Chief Financial Officer'; supporting = 'Chief Investment Officer, Board Governance Lead' (the Board Governance Lead carries the board-approval interaction). Apply the same normalization to F-12-04-S06 supporting ('Chief Financial Officer, Board Governance Lead').
rationale: Invalid role tokens orphan the step from the role model; board approval of the investment policy is required annually under the NAIC investment model acts, so the board interface should map to a real role. Fixing S01 alone would leave the identical defect on S06.

issue: Supporting includes 'Trader', which is not in the role inventory.
proposedFix: Supporting = 'Portfolio Manager, Chief Investment Officer' (or add a Trader/Execution role to the inventory if a dealing desk genuinely exists at Meridian).
rationale: Every step role must resolve to the 261-role inventory; Portfolio Manager is the closest practitioner who places orders in the current model.

issue: Supporting 'Custodian' is an external counterparty (custodian bank), not an internal role, and is not in the role inventory.
proposedFix: Supporting = 'Investment Operations Manager' (who manages the custodian interface); reference the custodian bank in inputs ('custodian confirmations') rather than as a role.
rationale: External parties belong in inputs/outputs, not the RACI; Investment Operations Manager is the inventory role that owns settlement and custody interaction day-to-day.

issue: Supporting 'Statutory Accountant' is not in the role inventory.
proposedFix: Supporting = 'Statutory Reporting Analyst, Senior Accountant'.
rationale: Direct inventory equivalents exist; statutory valuation (amortized cost vs fair value by NAIC designation) is exactly the Statutory Reporting Analyst's remit.

issue: Lead 'Business Requestor' is not a role in the inventory — it is a placeholder for whoever submits the request (it also appears as supporting on CS-08-02-S03).
proposedFix: Lead = 'Contract Administrator' (intake owner of contract requests); supporting = 'Contracts Manager'. The requesting business unit is captured in inputs, not as a role.
rationale: A step cannot be led by an undefined placeholder; Contract Administrator exists in the inventory and is the standard intake role in a contract lifecycle process.

issue: Lead 'Legal Counsel' (also supporting on S02) is not an inventory role — the inventory only has specialized counsel roles (Coverage, Litigation, Privacy, Regulatory) and General Counsel.
proposedFix: Lead = 'General Counsel' for negotiation sign-off with supporting = 'Contracts Manager, Paralegal'; or add a 'Commercial Counsel' role to the inventory if commercial contract volume warrants a dedicated practitioner.
rationale: Generic 'Legal Counsel' breaks role resolution; the inventory gap for commercial/transactional counsel at a carrier of this size is itself worth surfacing to the model owners.

issue: Supporting tokens 'Approval chain' (S04), 'Signatories' (S05), and 'Business Owner' (S06) are not roles in the inventory.
proposedFix: S04 supporting = 'General Counsel, Chief Financial Officer'; S05 supporting = 'Corporate Secretary'; S06 supporting = 'Contract Administrator'.
rationale: Three consecutive steps in this L4 reference undefined role placeholders, making the entire approval-execution-obligation chain unmappable to people; all three have direct inventory equivalents.

issue: L4 'Model registry & versioning' (TD-29-05) is sequenced after 'Model deployment & serving' (TD-29-04), but its own output is 'Registered models, version history, promotion gates' — which TD-29-04 consumes ('Validated models' input). Registry promotion is the gate that triggers deployment, not a post-deployment activity.
proposedFix: Reorder so registry & versioning precedes deployment & serving (registry between TD-29-03 CI/CD and TD-29-04 deployment), or at minimum make TD-29-04-S01's inputs explicitly reference registered/promoted models from TD-29-05.
rationale: Google Cloud's MLOps reference architecture and standard model-registry practice place registration and stage-promotion (staging → production) before deployment; deploying unregistered models defeats the promotion-gate control the registry exists to provide.

issue: Steps S07–S12 of RC-20-02 ('Develop Audit Plan' through 'Track Remediation') embed the complete internal audit lifecycle inside the compliance 'Control Monitoring' L4, duplicating the dedicated Audit & Assurance stream (RC-19-01 Audit Planning, RC-19-02 Fieldwork & Testing, RC-19-03 Reporting, RC-19-04 Issue Follow-up) — verified: all four RC-19 L4s exist in the outline.
proposedFix: Remove S07–S12 from RC-20-02 (the audit lifecycle already lives in RC-19) and end the L4 at S06 'Report to Governance'; if any unique content exists, merge it into RC-19.
rationale: Internal audit is the third line and must be organizationally independent of the compliance (second-line) function per the IIA Three Lines Model and IIA Standards; modeling audit planning/fieldwork/reporting inside compliance control monitoring both duplicates RC-19 and misstates the independence a regulator or external QA review would test.

issue: All five RC-20-04 steps are led by 'Chief Risk Officer (CRO)' — a string that does not match the role inventory (which has 'Chief Risk Officer'), and a CRO does not run day-to-day remediation tracking and report assembly. Verified verbatim in the outline for S01–S05.
proposedFix: Set lead to 'Operational Risk Manager' with supporting 'Chief Risk Officer, Model Risk Manager' across RC-20-04-S01..S05.
rationale: Leads should be the practitioner role executing the step; executive accountability belongs in supporting/oversight. The '(CRO)' suffix also breaks role-name matching against the inventory.

issue: RC-20-01 lead/supporting values include non-inventory, non-role strings — verified verbatim: 'Risk Analysts' (plural, S01), 'Business Units' (S01, S05), 'Business Risk Owners' (S02), 'Control Owners' (S03), 'Risk Owner' (S04 lead), 'Board Risk Committee' (S06), plus 'Internal Auditor' (S03; inventory has 'Internal Audit').
proposedFix: Map to inventory roles: 'Risk Analyst', 'Operational Risk Manager', 'Internal Audit'; make S04 lead 'Enterprise Risk Manager'; for S06 keep lead 'Chief Risk Officer' with supporting 'Corporate Secretary, Board Governance Lead' to represent board interaction.
rationale: Abstract groups and committees are not roles; they break the model's role-resolution (leads/supporting drive deliverable-role-task chains) and cannot be staffed or analyzed. All replacement names exist exactly in role-inventory.json.

issue: CI-05-02 uses roles absent from the inventory — verified verbatim: 'Reinsurance Broker' (S03, S04 — an external counterparty, not an internal role), 'Legal Counsel' (S05), 'Data Analyst' (S06), and 'CFO' (S02, S04 — inventory has 'Chief Financial Officer').
proposedFix: S03/S04 supporting → 'Broker Relationship Mgr, Ceded Reinsurance Analyst' (broker is the external channel, managed internally); S05 supporting → 'Contracts Manager, General Counsel'; S06 supporting → 'Reinsurance Manager, Data Steward'; expand 'CFO' → 'Chief Financial Officer'.
rationale: External parties and abbreviations not in role-inventory.json break role matching; the internal role accountable for broker interaction should be modeled instead of the broker itself. All replacement names exist exactly in the inventory.

issue: 'AR/AP Specialist' (CI-05-03-S06 supporting) and 'Statutory Accountant' (CI-05-04-S05 supporting) are not in the role inventory; 'Data Analyst' also appears at CI-05-03-S04 supporting. All three verified verbatim in the outline.
proposedFix: Replace 'AR/AP Specialist' with 'AR Reconciliation Analyst' (or 'Cash Application Specialist'), 'Statutory Accountant' with 'Statutory Reporting Analyst', and 'Data Analyst' (CI-05-03-S04) with 'Data Steward'.
rationale: Near-miss role names silently orphan these steps from the inventory-driven role/deliverable chains; exact inventory names ('AR Reconciliation Analyst', 'Cash Application Specialist', 'Statutory Reporting Analyst', 'Data Steward') exist for each function.

issue: Every OT-15-01/02/03 step is led by 'Production Support' (and it appears in OT-15-04 supporting), and OT-15-04 supporting includes 'Underwriting Operations Manager' — neither string is in the role inventory (which has 'Prod Support' and 'UW Operations Manager'). Verified: all 20 steps of the stream carry at least one of these variants.
proposedFix: Normalize lead to the inventory's 'Prod Support' (or rename the inventory entry once, consistently) and 'Underwriting Operations Manager' to 'UW Operations Manager' across OT-15-01-S01..OT-15-04-S05.
rationale: All 20 of this stream's steps fail role-inventory resolution because of these two name variants, so the entire stream drops out of role-based drill-downs and workforce analysis.

issue: OT-15-04 'Release Readiness & Hypercare' reuses incident-management step names ('Detect & Log', 'Triage & Assign', 'Investigate & Act', 'Resolve & Verify', 'Close & Report' — verified identical to OT-15-02's incident steps) for what is a planned, proactive readiness/transition activity — there is nothing to 'detect' in assessing deployment plans and support models.
proposedFix: Rename to a transition-shaped sequence, e.g. S01 'Assess Release & Support Readiness', S02 'Plan Hypercare & Cutover Support', S03 'Execute Hypercare Support', S04 'Verify Stability & Exit Criteria', S05 'Accept Service & Hand Over'.
rationale: ITIL 4 distinguishes service transition/validation from incident management; reactive verb framing misleads users of the model about the nature of the work and obscures the readiness-gate decision the L4's purpose implies.

issue: The L4 'Standards, reusable services and platform guardrails' (T-23-03) uses the incident/case-handling template (Detect & Log → Triage & Assign → Investigate & Act → Resolve & Verify → Close & Report) for what is a definitional, publish-and-govern process. Defining platform standards and guardrails is not triggered by detected events, and 'Detect & Log' makes no sense as the first step of authoring standards.
proposedFix: Re-template T-23-03 steps to the definitional flow used by its sibling L4s T-23-01/T-23-02: Define Requirements → Develop Approach → Build & Configure → Validate & Review → Approve & Publish, keeping the existing leads (Platform Engineering Lead) and the existing S05 outputs (platform standards, guardrails, reusable patterns, lifecycle decisions).
rationale: TOGAF's standards/architecture content lifecycle and COBIT APO03 treat standards definition as a develop-review-approve-publish cycle, not detect-triage-resolve. Verified in the outline: T-23-03-S02's desc is 'Triage severity and assign ownership' for a standards catalog, which breaks the inputs/outputs chain semantics and would confuse any practitioner walking the model.

issue: Across OC-13-01, six of the named roles do not exist in role-inventory.json: 'Procurement Manager' (leads S01/S02/S05), 'Business Requestor' (S01/S06), 'Legal Counsel' (S03), 'AP Specialist' (S05), 'IT Support' (S05), 'IT Security' (S02). Verified against the 261-role inventory — none of the six are present; every other L4 in both assigned streams uses inventory roles, making this L4 the outlier.
proposedFix: Remap to inventory roles: leads for S01/S02/S05 → Vendor Manager; S01/S06 supporting 'Business Requestor' → Business Analyst; S02 supporting 'IT Security' → Security Analyst (keep Compliance Analyst); S03 supporting 'Legal Counsel' → General Counsel (keep Contracts Manager as lead); S05 supporting 'AP Specialist, IT Support' → Vendor Coordinator, IT Service Desk Analyst.
rationale: Role-to-step resolution (deliverables, tasks, RACI views) silently drops steps whose roles are not in the 261-role inventory, so these six steps are invisible in role drill-downs and headcount/capacity analysis — a data-integrity defect, not a style preference. All proposed replacement names verified present in role-inventory.json.
sources: role-inventory.json (261 valid roles; none of the six names present)

issue: OC-13-01 'Vendor demand intake and selection' overruns its scope: S03 (Negotiate Contract) and S04 (Execute Contract) duplicate OC-13-02 'Risk review and contract finalization' (whose S05 output is 'negotiated contract'), and S06 (Monitor Performance — 'Track vendor delivery and SLAs') duplicates the entire OC-13-03 'Service review and SLA governance' L4. The same contract is negotiated/finalized in two L4s and SLA monitoring lives in two places.
proposedFix: End OC-13-01 at selection and onboarding: keep S01 (Identify Vendor Need), S02 (Conduct Due Diligence), the new sanctions-screening step, and S05 (Onboard Vendor, renumbered after contract execution in OC-13-02); move/merge S03-S04 contracting outputs into OC-13-02 as the single contracting home; delete S06 and hand off to OC-13-03 via an explicit output ('vendor setup complete, monitoring handover to service review').
rationale: The 2023 Interagency TPRM Guidance defines discrete lifecycle stages — planning, due diligence & selection, contract negotiation, ongoing monitoring, termination — and the model's own L3s mirror them (Vendor Sourcing / Due Diligence & Contracting / Performance Management / Risk & Exit Management). Having sourcing also perform contracting and monitoring breaks the stage boundaries, double-counts the deliverable chain, and creates ambiguous ownership between Vendor Manager and Contracts Manager.
